nodes.name: Error Triggered
nodes.notes: Registered as the error workflow for the orchestrator, document intake, and SLA escalation workflows. Receives the failed execution's context when any node exhausts its retries.

nodes.name: Workflow Settings
nodes.notes: Only place configuration is declared. The secret is read from the container environment by expression so it is never written into this workflow file.

nodes.name: Interpret Error
nodes.notes: Normalises the error trigger payload into the incident schema.

nodes.name: Record Incident
nodes.notes: Writes a platform incident row. No case_id means it appears in the recent-events view and no case timeline, which is correct for an orchestration failure that never resolved a case.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({event_type: 'RETRY_EXHAUSTED', case_id: Number($json.case_id), timestamp: new Date().toISOString(), data: Object.assign({_workflow: $workflow.name, _execution_id: $execution.id}, ({stage: 'error_handler', detail: 'Incident recording failed after 3 attempts; the original workflow failure is now invisible in the audit trail.'}))}) }}

nodes.name: Record Incident Failure
nodes.notes: Terminal. If even the error handler cannot record, the failure is silent.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({event_type: 'WORKFLOW_COMPLETED', case_id: Number($json.case_id), timestamp: new Date().toISOString(), data: Object.assign({_workflow: $workflow.name, _execution_id: $execution.id}, ({outcome: 'incident_recorded', workflow: $json.workflow, node: $json.node, case_id: $json.case_id}))}) }}

nodes.name: Record Incident Success
nodes.notes: Terminal success. The platform incident is visible in the recent-events view.

parameters.content:
## Vendor Onboarding — Error Handler

Registered as the error workflow for the other orchestration workflows. When any node in those workflows exhausts its retries, this workflow receives the execution context and records a platform incident.

**This workflow does not retry the failed work.** It records the fact that the orchestration layer itself failed, so platform operators can see it in the recent-events view. The original work must be retried by a human (or by re-triggering the upstream webhook) once the root cause is fixed.
